title: Package entry
summary: This file turns the `rag` folder into a Python package and decides what it exposes at the top level. It re-exports the two names most callers need, `RAGPipeline` (the whole system) and `Answer` (what a question returns), so you can write `from rag import RAGPipeline`. Nothing in the RAG pipeline runs here; it only wires names together.

key_ideas.explain: Python runs this file the first time anything imports `rag`. Whatever it imports becomes available as `rag.<name>`.
Re-exporting a small set of names hides the internal module layout. Callers depend on `rag.RAGPipeline`, not on the fact that it lives in `rag/pipeline.py`.

blocks.note: The module docstring. It describes the whole package in one line: bilingual question answering over documents, with citations. Tools like `help(rag)` show it.

A **relative import** (the leading dot means "from this same package"). It pulls `Answer` and `RAGPipeline` out of `rag/pipeline.py` so they are reachable as `rag.Answer` and `rag.RAGPipeline`. Note that importing `rag` therefore also imports the pipeline module and everything it imports (retrieval, FAISS, numpy), but not the heavy models, which are loaded lazily later.
`__all__` lists the public names. It controls what `from rag import *` brings in, and it tells linters and readers which names are the supported API.
A version string for the package. The FastAPI app in `rag/api.py` also reports version `1.0.0`; keeping one obvious place for it helps when you publish or debug a deployment.
